summary: This program builds a shopping list, then edits it in three ways: replacing an item by its position, adding a new item at the end, and removing an item by name. It finishes by printing every item and then reaching for the first and last one directly.

lines.text: A list holds several values in one variable, in the order you wrote them. Square brackets create the list and commas separate the items.

lines.code: shopping_list[4] = "chouriço"  # Replace snacks with Portuguese sausage
lines.text: Positions in a list start counting at 0, so index 4 is the fifth item, "snacks". Assigning to that position overwrites the old value in place.

lines.code: shopping_list.append("pastéis de nata")  # Portuguese custard tarts
lines.text: The append method adds one new item to the end of the list, growing it from seven items to eight.
Unlike indexing, remove searches for a matching value and deletes the first one it finds, so you do not need to know where it sits.
A for loop visits each item in turn, storing it in the variable item so the indented line below can use it.
Passing two values to print puts a space between them, which produces a neat dash before each item.
An f-string lets you drop an expression inside braces straight into the text, and \n adds a blank line before it for spacing.
Negative indexes count backwards from the end, so -1 is always the final item no matter how long the list has become.
